question: Will Lula win the most votes in the first round of the 2026 Brazil presidential election?
resolution_criteria:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the first round of this election.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

## Lula and the 2026 Brazil first round: research as of 2026-09-24

The polls available by 2026-09-24 had Lula narrowly ahead in the first round. Lula's lead over Flávio Bolsonaro was 2 to 4 points, close to the margins of error. Polymarket had moved in Flávio's favour for the overall election from 11 September. I found no first-round market price.

### 1. Resolution source
- The outcome is decided by the official TSE results (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br) or a consensus of credible reporting. The first round is on 2026-10-04, so no results existed by 2026-09-24. I did not fetch the TSE portal because it would not show anything yet.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Every poll I found from on or before 2026-09-24 shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), but within or close to the margin of error.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-24: Datafolha (2,002 interviews, 22-23 Sept, registered as BR-00304/2026, margin ±2) had Lula 40%, Flávio 36%, Augusto Cury 5%, Ronaldo Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 3%, Romeu Zema 1%. Blank, null or none was 5% and undecided 2%. Datafolha's previous poll (17 Sept) had Lula 39%, Flávio 36%. Most reports put the runoff at Lula 47%, Flávio 45%. This poll may have come out after the forecast closed at 03:40 UTC. [Jornal Opção](https://www.jornalopcao.com.br/ultimas-noticias/datafolha-lula-tem-40-e-flavio-bolsonaro-36-no-1o-turno-871618/), [SBT News](https://sbtnews.sbt.com.br/noticia/politica/datafolha-lula-tem-40-contra-36-de-flavio-no-1-turno)
- 2026-09-22 (approximate): an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll had Lula 45.8%, Flávio 43.4% in the first round and a runoff of 47.7% to 47.4%. Bloomberg Línea called it a technical tie. I could not confirm the exact release date. [Itatiaia](https://www.itatiaia.com.br/politica/eleicoes/atlas-bloomberg-flavio-bolsonaro-cresce-e-empata-com-lula-em-eventual-2-turno/)
- 2026-09-21: Quaest for Globo (2,004 interviews, 17-20 Sept, margin ±2) had Lula 37%, Flávio 33% in the first round. Lula was up 1 point and Flávio up 2 from Quaest's previous poll. The runoff was tied at about Flávio 42%, Lula 41%. [Brasil de Fato](https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/09/21/quaest-lula-vence-no-1o-turno-cenario-de-2o-turno-tem-empate-com-flavio-bolsonaro/)
- Mid-September: an AtlasIntel poll with fieldwork on 11-16 Sept had Flávio slightly ahead in the runoff, 47.2% to 46.8%. [Congresso em Foco / search snippet](https://congressoemfoco.com.br/noticia/120849/atlasintel-lula-abre-9-pontos-sobre-flavio-e-vence-todos-no-2-turno)
- Earlier in 2026: Flávio entered the race in December 2025 with his father's backing. He lost ground in May after audio sent to banker Daniel Vorcaro was released. Flávio denies any wrongdoing. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/6/flavio-bolsonaro-enters-brazils-2026-presidential-race-with-fathers-nod), [O Antagonista](https://oantagonista.com.br/brasil/flavio-cai-13-pontos-no-polymarket-apos-divulgacao-de-audio-enviado-a-vorcaro/)

### 4. Base rates
These are from my own background knowledge. I did not check them against sources in this session.
- The PT candidate topped the first round in 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014 and 2022, and finished second in 2018 behind Jair Bolsonaro.
- 2022: Lula won the first round 48.4% to 43.2%. The final polls overstated his margin, because Bolsonaro outperformed his polling by several points.
- Taken together, Brazilian polls have tended to underestimate the Bolsonaro-aligned candidate. A 2-4 point poll lead is about the size of that past error.

### 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-11: Polymarket's overall-election market had Flávio 52.45%, Lula 45.50%. Lula had led in all 120 readings from 14 May to 10 September. [Tribuna do Planalto](https://tribunadoplanalto.com.br/apostas-no-exterior-registram-alta-de-flavio-e-recuo-de-lula-em-setembro/)
- 2026-09-18: Polymarket had Flávio 54.8%, Lula 42.5%. [Tribuna do Planalto](https://tribunadoplanalto.com.br/apostas-no-exterior-registram-alta-de-flavio-e-recuo-de-lula-em-setembro/)
- Late September: Polymarket reportedly had Flávio about 58%, Lula 42%. The exact date is unclear and may be after 2026-09-24. [Revista Oeste](https://revistaoeste.com/politica/flavio-supera-lula-no-polymarket-e-elon-musk-reage/)
- These prices are for winning the presidency, not for topping the first round. I could not find a dated Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold price for the first-round question. Prediction markets on politics have been banned in Brazil since spring 2026. [Aos Fatos](https://www.aosfatos.org/noticias/pesquisa-flavio-61-intencoes-voto/)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls before 4 October, including final pre-election releases. In the polls above, Flávio has been gaining slightly faster than Lula.
- Late-campaign TV debates. Agência Lupa notes that a debate is shaping the closing themes. [Lupa](https://agencialupa.substack.com/p/13512680_lente-nas-elei-es-8)
- Smaller candidates (Cury, Caiado, Santos, Zema) may lose voters to the two leaders through tactical "useful vote" switching.
- First round on 2026-10-04, with the TSE count published the same night.

(e) **Scenarios.**

- **Yes:** Lula's base holds at about 43-45% of valid votes. The right's vote stays partly split among the minor candidates, and the polling error is small, as AtlasIntel's was in 2022. Lula finishes first by 1 to 3 points and the race goes to a close runoff.

(f) **From base rate to forecast.** I start at about 55%, since a polling lead discounted for Brazil's known bias is still a lead. I then move down about 7 points for three reasons:
- Momentum is toward Flávio.
- The minor-candidate vote that can still move leans right, so a squeeze favours Flávio.
- The most accurate pollster from 2022 shows only a 2.4-point gap.

The polling-error and squeeze reasons partly overlap, so I avoid going lower. Lula does still lead every poll.

Probability: 47%

- AtlasIntel, which was the most accurate pollster in 2022, shows only a 2.4-point gap.
  - Flávio gained slightly faster than Lula in Quaest's latest poll.
  - The historical polling bias toward Lula is about as large as his current lead.
  - Some smaller candidates are right-of-centre, mainly Caiado, Zema and Renan Santos (about 8% combined). Their voters are likely to switch tactically to Flávio.
  - Polymarket moved to Flávio 52-58% for the overall election from 11 September. That is a runoff-heavy signal, but it shows momentum.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** Late consolidation of right-leaning voters behind Flávio, plus a repeat of the 2022-style shy-Bolsonaro polling error, turns a 3-point poll deficit into a 1-2 point first-round win for Flávio.
- **Yes:** Polls are closer to accurate this time. Datafolha and Quaest's 4-point lead mostly holds, and Lula finishes first by 2-5 points even if he then faces a tight runoff.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 60% after adjusting for polling bias. The average poll lead is about 3.5 points. A historical bias correction of 2-4 points, plus tactical consolidation of the small right-wing candidates, brings the expected lead down to about 0-1.5 points, with an uncertainty of about 4 points. That gives roughly 55-58%. The Polymarket shift toward Flávio pulls me down slightly, but the market covers the overall election rather than the first round, so I only nudge down. I end around 55%.

Probability: 55%

- **No:** Right-leaning minor-candidate voters move to Flávio in the final week. Shy-Bolsonaro polling error repeats at even half its 2022 size. Flávio finishes first, for example 45% to 44%.
- **Yes:** Lula's base holds near 45-46% of valid votes. Minor-candidate vote splits rather than fully consolidating. Polling error is modest, and Lula finishes first by 1-4 points before an uncertain runoff.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start around 80% for a consistent multi-poll leader. I cut heavily, about 20 points, for three reasons:
- the documented pro-Lula polling bias of 5+ margin points in 2018 and 2022;
- AtlasIntel's narrow 2.4-point gap;
- the momentum and consolidation risk on the right.

The overall-election market favouring Flávio is consistent with Lula still being more likely to lead round one, because Lula's first-round edge is larger than his runoff edge. So the market does not push me much lower. I land slightly above a coin flip.

Probability: 56%
